data.title: Sex-stratified immune patterns across the canine lifespan and short-term responses to geroprotective interventions
data.authors: Lai M; Xu F; Xu Y; Mironenkov A; Jin Y; Zhang S; Pan J; Li M; Deng B; Zhu JK; Lyu YX

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Dog (intact laboratory Beagles: 80-dog cross-sectional cohort ages 1-11; 24 young dogs for a 90-day intervention arm)
data.finding: In 24 young Beagles given a 90-day course of rapamycin, the SGLT2 inhibitor canagliflozin, or dietary restriction, rapamycin produced the broadest shift in blood cytokines of the three, while a separate cross-sectional cohort of 80 Beagles aged 1-11 showed that immune aging in dogs is non-linear and sex-stratified rather than a steady decline. Dogs are an increasingly used translational model for geroscience because of their size and lifespan diversity, so this adds a rare canine data point to the rapamycin-immune-aging picture; the authors flag the intervention findings as exploratory given small group sizes and endpoint-only measurements.
data.abstract_excerpt: Canine models are invaluable for translational geroscience, but natural sex-associated immune aging remains under investigated. Here, we characterize the age-associated hematologic and serum cytokine profiles in a controlled cross-sectional cohort of 80 intact laboratory Beagles spanning 1 to 11 years of age. Canine immune aging is heterogeneous and non-linear. While several absolute leukocyte counts declined with age before rising again in geriatric dogs, serum cytokines exhibited distinct, sex-stratified patterns.
